findings.evidence: "The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Reorder to show employee review before submission: move paragraph 3 before paragraph 2, so the employee reviews, submits, then receives confirmation email.
findings.location: How to Apply, second and third paragraphs
findings.violation: The sequence is contradictory - the employee cannot review and submit before processing finishes if the email arrives after processing is complete.

findings.evidence: "An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives."
findings.fix: Replace with "until the requester submits the missing documentation" or "until the requester provides the missing information."
findings.violation: Unclear whether "missing item" refers to documentation the requester must provide or something external; the phrasing suggests external delivery.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the company may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: Inconsistent voice - shifts from third person ("employees") used throughout to second person ("you") and first person plural ("we").

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status..."
findings.fix: Assign explicit roles: "Employees record the stipend item... Managers countersign within two business days... Finance reconciles..."
findings.violation: Uses "you" and "countersign" without specifying which role (employee, manager, or staff) performs each action.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Replace with a complete ordered list: "Completing the request requires confirming eligibility, uploading the receipt, obtaining manager approval, finance confirmation, and final submission."
findings.violation: Sentence is grammatically incomplete and vague; it names only two partial elements without clarifying the full sequence.

findings.evidence: "Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove the sentence or replace it with content specific to special cases that adds new information.
findings.violation: This sentence repeats verbatim from the Program Overview section, introducing unnecessary redundancy.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Delete these sentences; keep only "The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout."
findings.violation: These three sentences are unrelated to home-office equipment stipends and belong in different documents.

findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it" appears in both sections describing different publications.
findings.fix: Keep the phrase in one section only (Program Overview) and remove it from Questions and Updates, or replace with unique language specific to each section.
findings.location: Program Overview (first mention) and Questions and Updates (second mention)
findings.violation: The identical phrase is repeated in two separate sections, creating redundancy.
